group_assessment.counts_measured: PubMed esearch, 2026-08-10. Corresponding lipid group: 'Genest J[au]' 977, 'Genest J[au] AND WWOX' 2. Co-lead human-genetics group: 'Pajukanta P[au]' 174, with WWOX 2. Collaborating gene groups, counted separately because they are not the authors of record here: 'Aqeilan RI[au] AND WWOX' 65 of 137 total, 'Aldaz CM[au] AND WWOX' 38.
group_assessment.weighting: The observation and the interpretation do not carry the same weight here, and the counts show why. The lipid phenotyping — HPLC lipoprotein profiles, 2D-PAGGE ApoA-I subspecies, family segregation — comes from a group with 977 publications in exactly that domain and should be weighted as expert measurement. The WWOX interpretation comes from those same authors on their second WWOX paper; the gene expertise sits with the collaborators who supplied the mouse models (Aqeilan 65, Aldaz 38) and appears in the author list rather than in the framing. So: high confidence in the lipid measurements as measurements, ordinary confidence in what the paper concludes WWOX is doing. This is the mirror image of the WOREE literature, where gene expertise is high and the phenotype measurement is descriptive — and it is a reason to read this paper for its numbers rather than for its conclusions.
group_assessment.note: The research-group knowledge base is excluded from the public edition; this assessment rests only on the measured counts above and on the Methods.

field_density.note: A cardiovascular-genetics paper carrying primary WWOX molecular biology. Parity of sources applies in its usual direction: the functional characterisation of Wwox-null lipid handling exists here and not in the WOREE literature.

verbatim_locators.abstract_anchoring_waived: No locator is abstract-anchored, and none could be. The abstract states the conclusion 'WWOX disruption alters HDL and lipoprotein metabolism' without the distinction the whole reading turns on — that the liver-specific knockout does NOT lower circulating HDL. Every proposition below is either that distinction, a figure panel, a statistical qualification, or an author-declared limitation: precisely the material an abstract drops. Verified mechanically: all sixteen text and table snippets match the body and none matches the abstract.

entries.proposition: Deleting Wwox in hepatocytes does NOT lower circulating HDL-C in either sex — the central negative, and the reason 'strong evidence' does not transfer intact.
entries.snippet: sole deletion of Wwox in hepatocytes did not result in significant differences in HDL-C plasma concentrations in mice of both genders
entries.anchor: Results, 'Validation of gene expression changes on HDL- and TG-regulators in Wwoxhep−/− mice', closing paragraph

entries.proposition: The whole-body knockout does show the HDL phenotype, with reduced circulating ApoA-I.
entries.snippet: HPLC serum characterization revealed a marked reduction in HDL-C (Figure 5A), concomitant with a significant decrease in circulating ApoA-I levels
entries.anchor: Results, 'Impaired HDL biogenesis in Wwox null mice'

entries.proposition: The authors' first explanation for the gap between models is incomplete knockdown, not biology — which makes the liver-specific negative weaker evidence than it appears.
entries.snippet: Wwox levels were only reduced by 2.85 fold in female and 2.34 fold in male Wwoxhep−/− mice, which might be insufficient to decrease whole-body circulating HDL-C levels

entries.proposition: Their second explanation is that non-hepatocyte liver cells still express Wwox, diluting the knockout.
